pages.title: Run chunk generation in a host process, and keep the in-process pool as the fallback
pages.description: Status: accepted. Supersedes the rejection of "a separate generation process over a socket" in ADR 0002.

headings.text: Why ADR 0002's reasoning no longer applies
headings.excerpt: ADR 0002 rejected a separate process because it "loses both transferable ArrayBuffer and the shared registry bundle", and priced the bundle at 75 ms for eight workers against 540 ms reading from disk.

One transport interface. GenerationTransport is the surface GenerationPool and ShardedGenerationPool already have: run a task in a priority band, cancel waiting tasks, promote them, read counters and stats, destroy.
A result is copied through the channel and deserialized on the server's event loop. The cost per hop is measured in the slice 2 report.
Generated output. Every status body runs the same code in a worker, and which process hosted the worker cannot show in the result. The digests ADR 0002 specifies are checked across both transports.
A socket instead of an IPC channel. It would let the host run on another machine, which is the later remote tier. The transport interface is the seam for that, and nothing here needs it yet.

Two gates apply, and both have to pass. The first is this server's named permissions, in permissions.json. A vanilla command's node is minecraft.command.<name>, so /teleport needs minecraft.command.teleport.

headings.excerpt: The server deliberately leaves 5 commands unwired. The rule the project follows is worth stating plainly, because it decides what you see when you type one: an unwired command is not registered at all.

@jsprismarine/mcfunction loads .mcfunction files and function tags from the pack stack, compiles them once, and runs them against a command runner.
One command per line, written without a leading slash. A line is a comment when its first non-whitespace character is #, and blank lines are skipped. A line ending in \ continues into the next one.
A line whose first non-whitespace character is $ is a macro line. It carries one or more $(variable) substitutions, and the caller has to pass a compound with an entry for each.

/function <id> runs one function. /function #<namespace>:<tag> runs every function the tag names, in order, with nested tags expanded in place; a function named twice runs once, and a cycle between tags is reported and…
A run is bounded by the two gamerules Java bounds it with. Both were renamed in 1.21.11, so a guide written against maxCommandChainLength or maxCommandForkCount is stale.

Here is the whole loop: a datapack on disk, a macro, a tag, and watching it run. Functions come out of the pack stack, which every server builds, so the only setting involved is the one naming your pack.

headings.text: Why the gameplay rules come from Java
headings.excerpt: Mojang publishes Java Edition's gameplay rules as data a server reads at load time. Bedrock keeps much of the same material in the engine.

headings.text: What the server loads at startup
headings.excerpt: Every server builds its content from the pack stack, so everything on this page is running by default. There is no setting that turns it off.

@jsprismarine/loot parses the 1447 vanilla tables once into closures and rolls them against a context. It owns the table grammar only: pools, entries, rolls and the order the three levels of modifier apply in.
Java 26.3 registers nine loot_pool_entry_type members and this package implements all nine: item, tag, loot_table, dynamic, slots, empty, group, alternatives and sequence.
Here is where a table actually gets rolled. Every path goes through the same registry, so what /loot reports and what a block drops cannot disagree. Block drops.
A rolled result carries Java item identifiers. mapLootToBedrock translates a list through javaItemToBedrock and reports every reviewed loss rather than dropping it.
@jsprismarine/recipes reads Java's 2042 recipe files and implements all 22 serializers that RecipeSerializers registers in the 26.3 jar. Vanilla uses every one of them.
@jsprismarine/advancements parses the 1866 vanilla files into a tree with their rewards and requirements, and implements all 58 registered trigger types. Vanilla uses 54 of them across 4045 criteria.
Seventeen. The rest are parsed, indexed and ready, and nothing in this server ever raises them, because the subsystem that would know the event does not exist.
@jsprismarine/enchantments holds the 43 vanilla definitions, all 31 effect component types, the enchanting table draw and the anvil.

The server reads four of the 31 effect components today. damage_protection becomes the Enchantment Protection Factor of everything worn, folded one equipment slot at a time from zero, which is what makes four pieces of…

The enchanting table reproduces Java's draw: enchantmentCost for the three row costs, selectEnchantments for the picks, all three rows driven from one generator seeded with the player's own enchantment seed.

armor_effectiveness is the one effect component the server will not apply. Breach is the only enchantment that declares it, and whether Java multiplies the result against the armor value or against the armor toughness…

@jsprismarine/predicates is the shared grammar underneath loot, advancements and enchantments. It implements all 20 loot_condition_type members and all 42 loot_function_type members of 26.3, plus 23 int providers, 28…

The vanilla datapack ships 883 tag files over 20 registries. The big ones are block with 300, item with 236, worldgen/biome with 86, villager_trade with 73, entity_type with 49 and damage_type with 36.
A datapack of yours is the last member of the stack, so it wins. The mechanics are the ones you already know from Java, with one difference worth stating up front: outside tags, nothing merges.

Run from source when you are building add-ons or plugins, or changing JSPrismarine: pnpm run dev rebuilds the packages you edit and restarts the server with your changes. The steps below set up a checkout.
1.1 Node.js 26.4.0 or newer and pnpm 12 or newer. The terminal UI loads node:ffi by default on Node 26.9 or newer. Node versions 26.4 through 26.8 require --experimental-ffi.

Each entry under worlds is one world: its seed, the provider that stores it on disk and the preset that says which dimensions it has and how each one generates.
Write a world's seed as a string, as the examples above do. A Minecraft seed is a 64-bit integer and a JSON number is a double, which is exact only below 2^53.
